conventions.names: Functions and methods: TS lowerCamelCase, Python snake_case of the same words (ts is lowerCamel of py; check_api.py enforces it). Types: PascalCase, identical in both. Param and field keys here are the Python names; in TS they are lowerCamel, except inside casing wire types, which are snake_case in both.
conventions.params: kind positional params are positional in both languages. kind option params are the trailing options object in TS and keyword-only arguments in Python. required false means optional; default is the value used when omitted.
conventions.results: {result, errors} is an expected-failure value: TS {ok: true, value} | {ok: false, error: {code, message}}, Python Ok[T] | Err[Failure] (frozen dataclasses). errors is the closed code set; every code is in the events ErrorCode enum (what the log records) or the ApiErrorCode enum in schema/api.schema.json (what public calls return). Only ConfigError at setup is thrown (throws).
conventions.async: async true: TS returns a Promise, Python is async def. A stream is TS AsyncIterable, Python AsyncIterator.
conventions.refs: urn:threads:schema:events:v1 is spec/schema/events.v1.schema.json, urn:threads:schema:host-api:v1 is spec/schema/host-api/host-api.v1.schema.json, urn:threads:schema:conformance:v1 is spec/conformance/case.schema.json. #/types/X is a type in this file.
conventions.generics: Deps defaults to null (TS undefined, Python None); Output defaults to string (the final text). Agent<Deps, Output> carries both into RunContext and RunResult.
conventions.adapters: Model, Sandbox, MemoryProvider, KnowledgeProvider, ChannelAdapter and SearchBackend are protocols. Concrete factories (anthropic(), e2b(), mem0(), slack(), ...) live in adapter packages, take a secret() for credentials and return one of these.

core.doc: Pure library. Runtime dependency: zod / pydantic only. Names pending an npm/PyPI check.

host.doc: Channels, schedules, the HTTP API (spec/schema/host-api/) and the CLI.

choices.open: lists run() and stream() as core functions; README and Consequences write bot.run(task).
choices.choice: Methods on the agent only: agent.run(input, opts), agent.stream(input, opts). No top-level run().
choices.why: One way to run, as the README shows. (OpenAI Agents SDK uses run(agent, input); a method reads the same and needs no extra import.)

choices.open: Parameter passing style per language.
choices.choice: Required inputs are positional; everything else is one trailing options object in TS and keyword-only arguments in Python, with the same names (camelCase/snake_case) and defaults.
choices.why: Mirrors OpenAI Agents SDK (run(agent, input, {context, maxTurns, signal})) and Pydantic AI keyword args.

choices.open: Which store run() uses when none is given.
choices.choice: sqlite(".threads"), the same default threads dev uses. Tests pass sqlite(":memory:").
choices.why: The log is the truth (invariant 1): a run without a durable store couldn't resume, fork or save a case.

choices.open: gives fork(point, {input?, ...}); a thread handle has no agent to run with.
choices.choice: fork() returns a Thread handle on the new branch; continue it with agent.run(input, {thread: child}).
choices.why: Keeps the thread handle pure data and control; one run path.

choices.open: lists approve() but no way to refuse a challenge.
choices.choice: Thread.deny(challengeId, principal, {reason}).
choices.why: Approvals need both outcomes (approval_denied).

choices.open: gives resolveParked(key, resolution) and cancel() without a principal, yet effect_resolved{by: human} and cancel_requested require one.
choices.choice: Every Thread method that appends an event takes a required positional principal: approve, deny, answer, resolveParked, cancel, compact, setModel, setOutputStyle, setMode. Only agent.run()/stream() default it, to the local operator {api, local, operator}, so the two-line example stays two lines.
choices.why: The events they write carry the actor's principal; a control action must name who took it.

choices.open: spells mcp({url}) and mcp.stdio({command}).
choices.choice: One mcp({name, url | command, ...}); exactly one of url or command.
choices.why: mcp.stdio has no plain Python equivalent; one function is smaller.

choices.open: names both built-ins local() (memory item 6, knowledge item 8).
choices.choice: localMemory() and localKnowledge({paths}).
choices.why: One exported name can't be both.

choices.open: names ScriptedModel (a class) and a fake sandbox.
choices.choice: scriptedModel(script) and fakeSandbox(script) factories taking the conformance ModelScript and SandboxScript.
choices.why: Same factory shape as every other provider; the scripts are already specified.

choices.open: Whether agent() takes hooks directly.
choices.choice: No. Hooks, observers and extension tools come only through extension().
choices.why: One primitive, one ordering rule.

choices.open: spells on(filter, handler) without saying where it lives.
choices.choice: extension({on: {<event type> | "*": handler}}).
choices.why: Observers are extension code; no new top-level name.

choices.open: How an app tool reports an expected failure.
choices.choice: execute returns the output; a thrown error is recorded as an error tool_result the model sees. Framework APIs still return failures as values.
choices.why: Same as OpenAI Agents SDK; tool authors don't wrap every return.

choices.open: says web, git and browser tools need configuration but not where.
choices.choice: agent({web: {fetch, search}, git: {credential}, browser: {auth}}); sandbox tools come with sandbox.
choices.why: Config-first; no extra factory names.

choices.open: allows roles or principals per tool or effect class.
choices.choice: agent({approvers: Principal[]}) covering every ask; per-tool approvers deferred.
choices.why: Smallest form that meets the defaults (local operator for run(), nobody for channels).

choices.open: writes saveCase(name, {expect, external_effects}) in TS.
choices.choice: API options are camelCase in TS (externalEffects); wire data types (Budget, Principal, the host-api shapes) keep snake_case in both languages.
choices.why: AGENTS.md: TS accessors may be camelCase, wire bytes are snake_case.

choices.open: names stop_hook_exhausted, continuation_limit, the pinned turn_completed reason is stop_hook_limit; max_turns has no RunResult mapping.
choices.choice: stop_hook_limit everywhere (RunResult, the onStop limit, ADRs 0012 and 0014 corrected); failed.error.code also adds max_turns and the pre-dispatch codes that end a run (host-api RunErrorCode).
choices.why: Pinned wire names win.

choices.open: gives before_tool_result pass | redact | block and before_input inject; hook_decision.decision has no pass, block or inject.
choices.choice: One vocabulary, the wire hook_decision.decision enum: beforeToolResult proceed | redact(spans) | deny, beforeInput allow | deny(reason), beforeModel proceed | deny(reason). Injections are a separate list on allow/proceed, recorded as injected{source: hook}. corrected to match.
choices.why: Docs, api.json and the wire agree.

choices.open: says callers are authenticated as principals, not how.
choices.choice: host({authenticate: (request) => Principal | null}); without it every /v1 route is 401.
choices.why: Secure by default; the app owns its auth.

choices.open: Whether POST /v1/runs waits for the result.
choices.choice: It returns 202 with {thread_id, branch_id} once the user_input is durable; the result arrives as the final SSE message.
choices.why: Runs can park for hours; HTTP requests shouldn't.

choices.open: lists store among provider interfaces; allows only SQLite in v0.1.
choices.choice: Store is opaque in v0.1: sqlite() is the only implementation and no methods are public.
choices.why: Don't freeze an interface nobody implements yet.

agent.doc: Describe an agent. Pure: no I/O, no env reads, no sockets. Checked by Agent.check() or on the first run.

params.name: browser

params.name: output_styles

tool.doc: Define an app tool. Input and output types are inferred from the schemas.

params.name: input
params.doc: Tool arguments are parsed with it at the boundary; its JSON Schema is the pinned input_schema.

params.name: output
params.doc: Pinned output_schema. A result that fails it is an error result; the effect still happened.

params.name: runs
params.doc: Required, no default.

params.name: execute
params.doc: runs host: required. The value is the result; a thrown error becomes an error tool_result the model sees.

params.name: module
params.doc: runs sandbox: required. Path of the module uploaded into the sandbox; JSON on stdin and stdout.

params.name: entrypoint
params.doc: runs sandbox: the function the module exposes.

params.name: effect
params.doc: . Undeclared tools are unguarded: uncertainty always parks.

params.name: dedup_window_ms
params.doc: Required exactly when effect is idempotent.

params.name: lookup
params.doc: Required when effect is reconcilable.

params.name: lookup_final
params.doc: Whether lookup's not_found is final under the provider's contract.

params.name: concurrent
params.doc: May run in parallel with other concurrent calls of one response (F1.1).

extension.doc: The one extension primitive: tools, trusted instructions and hooks. Trusted host code, not a security boundary.

params.name: name
params.doc: Unique; tools are namespaced <ext>__<tool>.

params.name: instructions
params.doc: Static; goes into line 0 after the base instructions.

params.name: on
params.doc: Observers keyed by event type, or "*". Committed events, delivered after append; can't block or change execution.

params.name: setup
params.doc: Runs once at check() or first run. Throwing is a ConfigError.

mcp.doc: An MCP server in one line. The host owns the connection and credentials; an unreachable server is a ConfigError naming it.

params.name: name
params.doc: Tools are named mcp__<name>__<tool>.

params.name: url
params.doc: Streamable HTTP (SSE fallback). Exactly one of url or command.

params.name: command
params.doc: stdio transport.

params.name: runs
params.doc: sandbox: stdio server inside the sandbox, with no host credentials.

params.name: tools
params.doc: Filter before pinning.

secret.doc: A reference to a host secret, resolved only in the host. Values never reach the log, prompts or the sandbox.

openThread.doc: A handle for inspection and control, independent of any in-memory run.

sqlite.doc: The one log and artifact store. Opens lazily: no I/O until first use.

params.name: path
params.doc: ":memory:" for a throwaway store (tests).

localMemory.doc: Built-in memory: SQLite FTS5 in the run's store.

localKnowledge.doc: Built-in knowledge: SQLite FTS5 over admitted versions stored as artifacts.

scriptedModel.doc: Test kit. Consumes the script in order, deterministic ids; a call past the end fails the run. The exact requests are in the log.

fakeSandbox.doc: Test kit. Runs the shared sandbox suite on every PR.

host.doc: Bind agents to a store, channels and schedules. Starts nothing until ready().

params.name: agents
params.doc: Keyed by the name channels, schedules and the HTTP API use.

params.name: authenticate
params.doc: Maps an HTTP API request to a principal, or null for 401. Absent: every /v1 route answers 401; channel webhooks still work.

run.doc: Run one input to a terminal result. Needs no server.

params.name: input
params.doc: Text or ordered input parts.

params.name: thread
params.doc: Continue this thread (a handle continues its branch). Absent: a new thread.

params.name: store
params.default_doc: the handle's store when thread is a Thread, else sqlite(".threads")

params.name: deps
params.doc: Host-only dependencies for tools and hooks (RunContext.deps). Never serialized. Required when Deps is not null.

params.name: budget
params.doc: Run budget, recorded on the user_input. Covers the thread and every descendant.

params.name: principal
params.doc: The verified sender of this input.

params.name: signal
params.doc: Local cancellation. Python uses task cancellation. Durable cancellation is Thread.cancel().

check.doc: Validate the definition and resolve setup (secrets, MCP handshakes, capabilities) without starting a run.

RunResult.doc: The HTTP form is host-api RunOutcome (ids instead of handles).

call_id.doc: Set inside a tool or tool hook.

effect_key.doc: <branch_id>:<call_id>; send it to providers that dedup.

timeline.doc: Every step with the exact request the model saw; fork points marked (F13.1).

fork.doc: A new branch restored into an isolated sandbox. Continue it with agent.run(input, {thread: child}).

params.name: external_effects
params.doc: The effects policy is required; stub is the only one.

params.name: at
params.default_doc: the latest fork point of the branch

params.name: dir
params.doc: Directory in the app repo; the case is <dir>/<name>/.

replay.doc: render(reduce(prefix)) equals every recorded request, with zero outbound calls (F13.6).

params.name: remember_rule
params.doc: One of the challenge's suggested_rules.

params.name: principal
params.doc: Who takes this action; recorded as the event's actor and authorized by the host.

params.doc: Who takes this action; recorded as the event's actor and authorized by the host.

setModel.doc: settings_changed{reason: user}. forbidden also covers a before_model_switch deny.

params.name: principal
params.doc: Who takes this action; recorded as the event's actor and authorized by the host.

params.doc: Who takes this action; recorded as the event's actor and authorized by the host.

params.name: tree
params.doc: Add descendants from their logs.

Thread.doc: A thread positioned at one branch. Every method reads or appends through the store; none needs the agent in memory.

portable.doc: false when the case depends on a named provider.

injections.doc: Recorded as injected{source: hook} events; not a decision.
Recorded as injected{source: hook} events; not a decision.

Hooks.doc: Every hook is optional, awaited and bounded by hook_timeout_ms. Decisions are {decision: <hook_decision.decision>, ...} objects. Injections are strings rendered as injected{source: hook}. A gating hook that throws or times out denies.

Tool.doc: An app tool (tool()). Carries Input, Output and Deps for inference.

Store.doc: The SQLite log and artifact store (sqlite()). Sealed in v0.1: no public methods.

Skill.doc: Loaded from the host config store, pinned by hash. Files in the sandbox are never skills.

ConfigError.doc: Thrown at setup only: TS class ConfigError extends Error, Python exception ConfigError. Every other expected failure is a value.

LookupResult.doc: An adapter's answer about an operation it may have performed. not_found is final only when the adapter declares it.

send.doc: Stream one attempt. A rejection before content is a rejected chunk, never a thrown error.

lookup.doc: Recover a response after a crash by client request id. Present when info.lookup.

Model.doc: What a model adapter package (anthropic(), openai(), ...) returns. One transport attempt per send; SDK retries off.

limits.doc: Window, output cap, billing bound and price.

accepts.doc: Input parts it accepts; others fail pre-dispatch with content_unsupported.

request_id.doc: Client request id, derived from the model_request event.

lookup.doc: Find a sandbox whose create response was lost. Present when info.lookup.

Sandbox.doc: What a sandbox adapter (e2b(), daytona(), modal(), fakeSandbox()) returns. Every create and restore carries an operation key written to the resource ledger first.

exec.doc: A timeout kills the whole process group.

params.name: env
params.doc: Exactly this env; nothing inherited.

snapshot.doc: Freeze or stop tracked processes, capture, thaw. Returns only once durable and restorable.

Scope.doc: From host config and the verified principal. Never a tool argument.

Binding.doc: Issued by the host; the provider stores it opaquely.

revision.doc: The store's monotonic revision after this ingest.

params.name: as_of
params.doc: Search as of this revision (a pinned fork).

SearchBackend.doc: A web_search backend adapter (Exa, Brave, Tavily).

agent.doc: The host agent key this channel routes to.

ChannelAdapter.doc: What a channel adapter (slack(), whatsapp(), github()) returns. verify, parse, ack and render are pure.

address.doc: Conversation key; the host maps it to a thread.
Conversation key; the host maps it to a thread.

asgi.doc: Mount in FastAPI or any ASGI server.

ready.doc: Confirms bindings. Sends nothing, starts no run.

stop.doc: Drains in-flight intake and releases leases.

Host.doc: TS: supports await using (Symbol.asyncDispose calls stop). Python: an async context manager (__aenter__ calls ready, __aexit__ calls stop).
